metas.name: Paterson
metas.description:
Captures a routine life as a work of art. One week with a bus driver named Paterson, in Paterson, who writes poems about matchboxes and waterfalls between shifts.

A quiet observation of the triumphs and defeats of daily life, along with the poetry evident in its smallest details.

metas.name: Tampopo
metas.description:
Captures food as craft, sex, comedy and social ritual all at once. A truck driver mentors a widow until her ramen is perfect, cut with vignettes of people eating in every possible way.

A truck driver stops at a small family-run noodle shop and decides to help its fledgling business. The story is intertwined with various vignettes about the relationship of love and food.

metas.name: Do the Right Thing
metas.description:
Captures a neighbourhood on the hottest day of the year. A Brooklyn block and a pizzeria wall of fame, everyone funny and aggrieved in their own direction until the heat does what heat does.

On the hottest day of the year on a street in the Bedford-Stuyvesant section of Brooklyn, everyone's hatred and bigotry smolder and build until violence erupts.

metas.name: Synecdoche, New York
metas.description:
Captures a life trying to represent itself honestly, and drowning in the attempt. A theatre director builds a scale copy of his city inside a warehouse and keeps casting people to play people, including himself, for decades.

A theater director struggles with his work and the women in his life as he creates a life-size replica of New York City inside a warehouse as part of his new play.

metas.name: Grey Gardens
metas.description:
Captures a mother and daughter fused together in a decaying mansion. The Beales, relatives of Jackie Kennedy, singing, bickering and feeding raccoons in the attic — performing for the camera and trapped with each other.

Meet a mother and daughter, high-society dropouts, reclusive cousins of Jackie O., managing to thrive together amid the decay and disorder of their East Hampton, NY, mansion, making for an eerily ramshackle echo of the American Ca...

metas.name: Dr. Strangelove
metas.description:
Captures nuclear annihilation as a bureaucratic procedure. Generals, presidents and advisors in rooms — vain, procedural and insane — while the world ends by checklist.

After a rogue U.S. general orders an unauthorized nuclear attack on the Soviet Union, leaders in the War Room race to prevent global catastrophe.

metas.name: The Death of Stalin
metas.description:
Captures absolute power as petty, terrified men improvising. Stalin drops dead and his inner circle plot, flatter and panic in the same breath — very funny, and people keep being shot between jokes.

Moscow, 1953. After being in power for nearly 30 years, Soviet dictator, Joseph Vissarionovich Stalin, takes ill and quickly dies. Now the members of the Council of Ministers scramble for power.

metas.name: Withnail and I
metas.description:
Captures the end of youth as squalor and one great friendship rotting. Two out-of-work actors in 1969 London, a disastrous country holiday, and one of them beginning to leave the other behind.

Two sloppy actors spend a weekend holiday at an uncle's country cottage.

metas.name: Election
metas.description:
Captures ambition so pure it becomes frightening, at a high school. A student election, a teacher who decides one candidate must be stopped, and everyone's voiceover giving their self-justifying version.

A high school teacher meets his match in an over-achieving student politician.

metas.name: Chungking Express
metas.description:
Captures city loneliness at pop speed. Hong Kong, two lovesick cops, expired pineapple cans, and a snack-bar girl breaking into a man's flat to clean it while 'California Dreamin'' loops.

Two melancholic Hong Kong policemen fall in love: one with a mysterious female underworld figure, the other with a beautiful and ethereal waitress at a late-night restaurant he frequents.

metas.name: Eighth Grade
metas.description:
Captures social anxiety in the age of front-facing cameras, exactly. A girl filming confident advice videos she cannot follow, pool parties endured minute by minute, and a father scene near the end that rearranges parents.

An introverted teenage girl tries to survive the last week of her disastrous eighth grade year before leaving to start high school.

metas.name: The Apartment
metas.description:
Captures loneliness in a big company, and kindness as a decision. An insurance clerk lends his flat to executives for their affairs to get promoted, loves the elevator girl from afar, and hits Christmas at the lowest point of both.

A Manhattan insurance clerk tries to rise in his company by letting its executives use his apartment for trysts, but office politics and his own romantic hopes complicate matters.

metas.name: Amélie
metas.description:
Captures a lonely young woman engineering small happinesses for strangers. Montmartre, a tin of childhood treasures returned to its owner, and a heroine who can fix everyone's life except ask for anything in her own.

Despite being caught in her imaginative world, young waitress Amelie decides to help people find happiness. Her quest to spread joy leads her on a journey during which she finds true love.

metas.name: Singin' in the Rain
metas.description:
Captures pure performed joy, inside a story about an industry panicking. Hollywood switching to sound, a star with a terrible voice, and musical numbers that still feel like showing off for the love of it.

When Hollywood's silent era gives way to talkies, a dashing screen idol and a gifted newcomer navigate romance, rivalry, and the comic chaos of reinventing the movies.

metas.name: Paddington 2
metas.description:
Captures decency as something contagious. A bear framed for stealing the pop-up book he wanted to buy his aunt, sent to prison — and the prison improves because he is in it.

Paddington, now happily settled with the Brown family and a popular member of the local community, picks up a series of odd jobs to buy the perfect present for his Aunt Lucy's 100th birthday, only for the gift to be stolen.

metas.name: Big Night
metas.description:
Captures two brothers arguing about whether a meal should be art or business. Italian immigrants, a failing restaurant, one elaborate dinner to save it, and a final wordless scene of one cooking breakfast for the other.

New Jersey, 1950s. Two brothers run an Italian restaurant. Business is not going well as a rival Italian restaurant is out-competing them. In a final effort to save the restaurant, the brothers plan to put on an evening of incredi...

metas.name: Rushmore
metas.description:
Captures a precocious teenager's grandiosity as a grief strategy. A scholarship kid who runs every club and stages huge plays falls for a widowed teacher and goes to war with a sad industrialist who is, emotionally, the same age.

A teenager at Rushmore Academy falls for a much older teacher and befriends a middle-aged industrialist. Later, he finds out that his love interest and his friend are having an affair, which prompts him to begin a vendetta.

metas.name: Day for Night
metas.description:
Captures a film set as a chaotic temporary family. Truffaut plays the director of a mediocre melodrama, keeping affairs, breakdowns, accidents and deadlines moving toward a finished film nobody thinks is great and everybody needs.

A committed film director struggles to complete his movie while coping with a myriad of crises, personal and professional, among the cast and crew.

metas.name: The Truman Show
metas.description:
Captures a paranoia that turns out to be an accurate description. An insurance salesman in a seaside town so pleasant it feels laminated, a sky that malfunctions, and a dawning suspicion about everyone who loves him.

An insurance salesman begins to suspect that his whole life is actually some sort of reality TV show.

metas.name: Lady Bird
metas.description:
Captures a mother and daughter who love each other in a way that keeps missing. Sacramento, a girl desperate to leave for the East Coast, a mother working double shifts, fights in moving cars, and a final voicemail that reframes every argument.

A fiercely independent teenager tries to make her own way in the world while wanting to get out of her hometown of Sacramento, California, and to get away from her complicated mother and recently-unemployed father.

metas.name: Secretary
metas.description:
Captures kink as, for one specific person, a form of self-knowledge. A young woman fresh out of hospital for self-harm takes a typing job with a demanding lawyer, in a relationship the film treats as tender rather than a diagnosis.

A timid young woman starts working for a demanding lawyer and finds a new way to deal with her self-harming urges.

metas.name: Touki Bouki
metas.description:
Captures two young people dreaming of Paris so hard the film itself starts hallucinating. Senegal: a cowherd and a student steal and scheme toward a ship, on a motorbike with a skull mounted on it, in editing that jumps like a skipping song.

Mory, a cowherd, and Anta, a university student, try to make money in order to go to Paris and leave their boring past behind.

metas.name: Hyenas
metas.description:
Captures a village discovering its price. A woman returns after decades, impossibly rich, offering her poor hometown a fortune for one act of 'justice' against the man who wronged her — while shops fill with goods bought on credit.

A now-rich woman returns to her poor desert hometown to propose a deal to the populace: her fortune, in exchange for the death of the man who years earlier abandoned her and left her with his child.

metas.name: Gummo
metas.description:
Captures boredom and poverty in an American town as unconnected afternoons. Xenia, Ohio, after a tornado: kids sniffing, selling dead cats, taped monologues, no plot arriving to save anyone.

Lonely residents of a tornado-stricken Ohio town wander the deserted landscape trying to fulfill their boring, nihilistic lives.

metas.name: Daisies
metas.description:
Captures two girls deciding the world is spoiled, so they'll be spoiled too. A Czech New Wave food-fight against everything — banquets wrecked, scissors, fire, a chandelier swing — anarchy as pure visual mischief.

After realizing that all world is spoiled, Marie and Marie are committed to be spoiled themselves. They rip off older men, feast in lavish meals and do all kinds of mischief. But what is all this leading to?

metas.name: Playtime
metas.description:
Captures modern architecture failing to be lived in. Tati wanders a Paris of glass and identical cubicles where the jokes happen at the edges of the frame, all at once, none of them underlined.

Monsieur Hulot curiously wanders around a high-tech Paris, paralleling a trip with a group of American tourists. Meanwhile, a nightclub/restaurant prepares its opening night, but it's still under construction.

metas.name: The Long Goodbye
metas.description:
Captures a decent man out of sync with his decade. Altman's Philip Marlowe shuffles through sunlit, corrupt Los Angeles in a rumpled suit, the last person still taking loyalty seriously.

Marlowe investigates a friend's alleged suicide, missing money and murder in 1970s Los Angeles.

metas.name: It's Such a Beautiful Day
metas.description:
Captures a mind coming apart, drawn with stick figures. Hertzfeldt narrates a man with a failing brain in three chapters — funny, fragmented, and by the end genuinely cosmic.

Bill struggles to put together his shattered psyche, in this new feature film version of Don Hertzfeldt's animated short film trilogy.

metas.name: Toni Erdmann
metas.description:
Captures a father trying to joke his daughter back to life. A prankster dad with false teeth infiltrates his consultant daughter's sterile Bucharest existence — a comedy that keeps tipping into grief and back.

A practical joking father tries to reconnect with his hard working daughter by creating an outrageous alter ego and posing as her CEO's life coach.

metas.name: The Favourite
metas.description:
Captures court power as intimate warfare. Two women compete to be Queen Anne's favourite — her bed, her ear, her rabbits — through fisheye candlelit corridors, with a lonely, raging queen at the centre.

In early 18th-century England, the status quo at the court is upset when a new servant arrives and endears herself to a frail Queen Anne.

metas.name: The Worst Person in the World
metas.description:
Captures turning thirty with every option still open and none chosen. Oslo in twelve chapters: a woman cycles through careers and men, including a night that pauses the entire city so she can test a life before living it.

The chronicles of four years in the life of Julie, a young woman who navigates the troubled waters of her love life and struggles to find her career path, leading her to take a realistic look at who she really is.

metas.name: The Banshees of Inisherin
metas.description:
Captures being dumped by a friend. One morning Colm simply doesn't want to talk to Pádraic anymore, and a whole island watches a small rejection escalate toward the mythic. Funny, until the exact moment it isn't.

Two lifelong friends find themselves at an impasse when one abruptly ends their relationship, with alarming consequences for both of them.

metas.name: Crumb
metas.description:
Captures how the same upbringing produces a famous artist, a broken man, and something in between. Cartoonist R. Crumb and his two brothers, all shaped by one brutal household, in Terry Zwigoff's unsparing family portrait.

An intimate portrait of controversial cartoonist Robert Crumb and his traumatized family.

metas.name: American Movie
metas.description:
Captures delusion and genuine talent living in the same person. Mark Borchardt, a Wisconsin sanitation worker with debts and a drinking problem, tries to finish a horror short to fund his dream feature — very funny until, suddenly, it isn't.

Aspiring filmmaker Mark Borchardt attempts to finance his dream project by finally completing Coven (1997), a micro-budget horror film he abandoned years before.

metas.name: Man Bites Dog
metas.director: Rémy Belvaux, André Bonzel, Benoît Poelvoorde
metas.description:
Captures the complicity problem pushed to its logical endpoint — the cluster's one fiction: a student crew follows a charming serial killer for a documentary, graduating from filming him, to holding the camera steady, to helping.

A film crew follows a ruthless thief and heartless killer as he goes about his daily routine. But complications set in when the film crew lose their objectivity and begin lending a hand.

metas.name: Sherman's March
metas.description:
Captures the personal documentary being invented out of failure. McElwee sets out to film Sherman's Civil War campaign, gets dumped before shooting starts, and the film becomes his disastrous search for love among old flames, narrated in a deadpan spiral.

Documentary filmmaker Ross McElwee sets out to make a movie about Union General Sherman's March to the Sea towards the end of the American Civil War, but keeps getting sidetracked by his own love life.

metas.name: Time of the Gypsies
metas.description:
Captures folk storytelling surviving, barely, inside modern crime. A Romani teenager with telekinetic powers is lured into a smuggling life in Italy, half narrated by Goran Bregović's score — Petrović's world taken into magical realism.

In this luminous tale set in the area around Sarajevo and in Italy, Perhan, an engaging young Romany (gypsy) with telekinetic powers, is seduced by the quick-cash world of petty crime, which threatens to destroy him and those he l...

metas.name: Ten Canoes
metas.description:
Captures oral tradition's actual structure. In Arnhem Land, an elder tells a young man a cautionary ancestral tale inside which another tale is told, while they hunt goose eggs in the swamp — stories nested for a practical moral purpose, with jokes.

In Australia's Northern Territory, a man tells us a story of his people and his land. It's about an older man, Minygululu, who has three wives and realizes that his younger brother Dayindi may try to steal away the youngest wife.

metas.name: Amarcord
metas.description:
Captures a community remembering itself, every ritual half affection and half mockery. Fellini rebuilds his hometown of Rimini as permanent carnival: fascist rallies, family dinners, a peacock in the snow, a whole town rowing out to greet an ocean liner.

A series of comedic and nostalgic vignettes set in a 1930s Italian coastal town.

metas.name: Calendar
metas.description:
Captures diaspora as a loop of beautiful images you can't live inside. Egoyan sends a Canadian photographer to Armenia to shoot twelve ancient churches for a calendar, his marriage failing in the car between sites — then the ritual repeats, reframed, back in Toronto.

A woman stays in Armenia after her photographer husband completes his assignment and returns home to Canada.

metas.name: The Cremator
metas.description:
Captures evil as a smiling civil servant. A Prague crematorium director absorbs Nazi ideology as a career opportunity and a philosophy of hygiene, in Karel Höger's unbearably gentle monotone.

Set in Central Europe during World War II, a demented cremator believes cremation relieves earthly suffering and sets out to save the world.

metas.name: Weekend
metas.description:
Captures a civilisation ending as a traffic jam. A bourgeois couple drives to collect an inheritance and the road fills with wrecks, corpses, cannibals and literary ghosts. Not the 2011 Weekend already at #145 — this is the other one, and it's feral.

A surreal tale of a married couple going on a road trip to visit the wife's parents with the intention of killing them for the inheritance.

metas.name: Céline and Julie Go Boating
metas.description:
Captures two women hacking a melodrama from the audience seats. A librarian and a magician find a haunted house where the same Victorian drama replays daily; they enter it, swap places with its characters and start stealing the plot with the help of magic sweets.

A mysteriously linked pair of young women find their daily lives preempted by a strange boudoir melodrama that plays itself out in a hallucinatory parallel reality.

metas.name: Save the Green Planet!
metas.description:
Captures a conspiracy theorist who might be right, played at full scream. A beekeeper kidnaps a chemicals CEO he believes is an alien prince; comedy, torture chamber, police procedural and apocalypse keep swapping places until the film lands somewhere genuinely sad.

Byeong-gu believes that the world is on the verge of an alien invasion, and sets out to save the world.

metas.name: Sherlock Jr.
metas.description:
Captures a projectionist climbing into the screen to fix the plot from inside. A century old and still the cleanest film ever made about wanting to live in the observed layer instead of the real one; the montage where the scenery changes around him mid-step has never been topped.

A film projectionist longs to be a detective, and puts his meagre skills to work when he is framed by a rival for stealing his girlfriend's father's pocketwatch.

metas.name: Sullivan's Travels
metas.description:
Captures a comedy director who goes slumming to learn suffering and learns the value of comedy instead. He disguises himself as a tramp to research a serious film, gets the research, and the conclusion lands in a prison screening room full of laughing men.

A Hollywood director sets out to experience life as a homeless person in order to gain relevant life experience for his next movie.

metas.name: Zelig
metas.description:
Captures a man whose personality is whoever is standing nearest. A mockumentary about a 1920s "human chameleon" who becomes a boxer beside boxers and a rabbi beside rabbis, assembled from fake newsreels and real historians playing along — conformity as a superpower and a diagnosis.

"Documentary" about a man who can look and act like whoever he's around, and meets various famous people.

metas.name: The Purple Rose of Cairo
metas.description:
Captures a film character noticing he's being watched, and stepping out. A Depression-era waitress goes to the same romance every day until its hero leaves the screen for her — and the other characters, stuck mid-plot, have to improvise without him.

During the Depression in 1935 New Jersey, a lonely waitress with an abusive husband who takes comfort from the movies is stunned when a movie character walks off the screen and into the real world, offering her the hope of a happi...

metas.name: Groundhog Day
metas.description:
Captures a loop that turns out to be a curriculum. It wasn't in your 363, which surprised me too. A weatherman relives one day until the day is no longer the constraint — the rare infinitely-referenced film that is also exactly as good as its reputation.

A curmudgeonly weatherman finds himself stuck in a time loop and is forced to relive the same day over and over again.

metas.name: Beyond the Infinite Two Minutes
metas.description:
Captures a café monitor that shows the room two minutes in the future. Shot on a phone in apparent single takes by a Kyoto theatre troupe; the staff keep feeding instructions to their past selves and the recursion stacks up like a card trick that keeps working.

A cafe owner discovers that the TV in his cafe suddenly shows images from the future, but only two minutes into the future.

metas.name: Being John Malkovich
metas.description:
Captures a portal into someone else's head, rented out at $200 a session. A puppeteer finds a door on floor 7½ that drops you behind Malkovich's eyes for fifteen minutes — the transducer problem played as office farce, then as tragedy.

A puppeteer discovers a portal that leads literally into the head of movie star John Malkovich.

metas.name: The Double
metas.description:
Captures a man replaced by the version of himself with better settings. A clerk nobody notices meets his double, who is identical and effortlessly everything he isn't; Dostoevsky rebuilt as a clanking bureaucratic nightmare with Jesse Eisenberg against himself.

The unenviable life of a government-agency clerk takes a horrific turn with the arrival of a new co-worker who is both his exact physical double and his opposite otherwise--he's a confident, charismatic ladies' man.

metas.name: The Science of Sleep
metas.description:
Captures dreams as a handmade TV studio inside a shy man's skull. A Mexican illustrator in Paris can't keep his dream-logic — cardboard cameras, cellophane water, a one-second time machine — from leaking into the courtship he's botching while awake.

A man entranced by his dreams and imagination is love-struck with a French woman and feels he can show her his world.

metas.name: Dave Made a Maze
metas.description:
Captures a living-room fort that is bigger, and lethal, inside. An artist builds a cardboard maze he claims he can't finish or escape; his girlfriend leads a rescue party in with documentary crew in tow. Every trap is cardboard. It kills people anyway.

Dave, an artist who has yet to complete anything significant in his career, builds a fort in his living room out of pure frustration, only to wind up trapped by the fantastical pitfalls, booby traps, and critters of his own creation.

metas.name: One Cut of the Dead
metas.description:
Captures a film set surviving its own film. The first half-hour is a wobbly one-take zombie short; then the film rewinds and shows you the production, and every wobble becomes a joke with a fuse on it. Engineered joy — don't read anything else about it.

Things go badly for a hack director and film crew shooting a low budget zombie movie in an abandoned WWII Japanese facility, when they are attacked by real zombies.

metas.name: Swiss Army Man
metas.description:
Captures a friendship with a corpse who is also a toolkit. A castaway rides a flatulent body to shore and teaches it how to be a person — jet-ski farts, earnest puppet dioramas of ordinary life, and a sincerity that sneaks up on the gross-out premise.

A hopeless man stranded on a deserted island befriends a dead body, and together they go on a surreal journey to get home.

metas.name: Everything Everywhere All at Once
metas.description:
Captures a multiverse used as a family argument. A laundromat owner audits her failed lives across universes — chef, starlet, rock, sausage-fingered pianist — and the loudest sci-fi machinery of the decade is aimed at a tax audit and a daughter. Absent from your 363; its absence was a gap, not a judgement.

A middle-aged Chinese immigrant is swept up into an insane adventure in which she alone can save existence by exploring other universes and connecting with the lives she could have led.

metas.name: Lars and the Real Girl
metas.description:
Captures a town agreeing, as treatment, to believe. A painfully shy man orders a life-size doll and introduces her as his girlfriend; on a doctor's advice the whole town plays along — church seat, volunteer shifts, the works. The premise sounds like a sketch; the execution is a study in communal gentleness.

A delusional young man strikes up an unconventional relationship with a doll he finds on the Internet.

metas.name: Brigsby Bear
metas.description:
Captures fandom as a survival structure. A man raised in a bunker on a fake children's show — hundreds of episodes made only for him — is rescued into a world where the show never existed, and decides the only sane response is to film its finale himself.

After being freed from his life in an underground bunker, a man sets out to make a movie of the only TV show he has ever known.

metas.name: What We Do in the Shadows
metas.description:
Captures four vampires failing at flatshare administration. Wellington's undead argue about the dishes roster, dress codes for clubs and a rival werewolf pack ("we're werewolves, not swearwolves") in deadpan documentary form. The lightest thing on this list, deliberately.

Viago, Deacon, and Vladislav are vampires who are struggling with the mundane aspects of modern life, like paying rent, keeping up with the chore wheel, trying to get into nightclubs, and overcoming flatmate conflicts.

metas.name: Ernest & Celestine
metas.director: Stéphane Aubier, Vincent Patar, Benjamin Renner
metas.description:
Captures a bear and a mouse outlawed by both their societies for the friendship. Bears live above, mice below, each raised on horror stories about the other; a watercolor heist and a double trial later, the film has made its whole case with a pencil line and a piano.

The story of an unlikely friendship between a bear, Ernest, and a young mouse named Celestine.

metas.name: Robot Dreams
metas.description:
Captures a friendship conducted entirely without dialogue, in 1980s New York, between a dog and a mail-order robot. They dance to Earth, Wind & Fire on roller skates; a beach closing separates them; the film then does the bravest thing a family film can do with its ending. Wordless, and it earns tears honestly.

The adventures and misfortunes of Dog and Robot in New York City during the 1980s.

metas.name: Marcel the Shell with Shoes On
metas.description:
Captures an inch-high shell with a breadcrumb for a hat, processing fame and loss at full sincerity. A documentarian films his tiny Airbnb cohabitant, whose missing community and ill grandmother turn stop-motion cuteness into something quietly devastating about scale and care.

A cash-strapped documentary maker decides to make his newest documentary about a mollusk shell he finds living in his Airbnb with his friends.

metas.name: An Actor's Revenge
metas.description:
Captures kabuki artifice turned into a weapon. An onnagata — a male actor who plays women — hunts the three men who destroyed his parents, never leaving character onstage or off; Ichikawa shoots it in widescreen tableaux where the theatrical sets and the "real" streets obey the same painted logic. Maximalism with a revenge plot for a spine.

Yukinojo, a Kabuki actor, seeks revenge by destroying the three men who caused the deaths of his parents. Also involved are the daughter of one of Yukinojo's targets, two master thieves, and a swordsman who himself is out to kill ...

metas.name: Sita Sings the Blues
metas.description:
Captures the Ramayana told four ways at once: 1920s blues vocals by Annette Hanshaw, shadow-puppet narrators bickering over the plot, lush vector animation, and the director's own breakup drawn in squiggles — the same story projected through four transducers, and they don't agree.

An animated version of the epic Indian tale of Ramayana set to the 1920s jazz vocals of Annette Hanshaw.

metas.name: Mind Game
metas.description:
Captures a failed manga artist dying, telling God off, and clawing back to life at maximum velocity. The style mutates per scene — rotoscope, crayon, photo-collage — and the finale is a many-minute sprint through every life he hasn't lived yet. The anti-grit entry: pure forward motion.

After a deadly encounter with two yakuza, a loser with a crush on his childhood girlfriend goes to heaven and back, embarking on a psychedelic self-discovery experience with her and his friends.

metas.name: World of Tomorrow
metas.description:
Captures a little girl visited by her own clone from 227 years later, who explains the future in a level, broken monotone. Seventeen minutes, stick figures, and the whole apparatus of memory-copying, failed immortality and inherited feeling. Your collection's shortest entries are 17 minutes; this is the other one that earns it.

A little girl is taken on a mind-bending tour of her distant future.

metas.name: Soul
metas.description:
Captures a jazz pianist who dies on the day of his break and has to argue his way out of the afterlife's intake office. The Great Before assigns personalities like case files; Joe's file keeps insisting the meaning was in the ordinary takes. Pixar's most explicit film about what a life is for, hidden inside its most musical one.

Joe is a middle-school band teacher whose life hasn't quite gone the way he expected. His true passion is jazz. But when he travels to another realm to help someone find their passion, he soon discovers what it means to have soul.

metas.name: Lily and Jim
metas.description:
Captures a blind date narrated by both daters at once, in split-screen stick figures, each privately misreading the other in real time. Thirteen minutes, made when he was barely out of film school, and the dual-internal-monologue structure is already fully his.

A blind date ends in disaster.

metas.name: Billy's Balloon
metas.description:
Captures toddlers being attacked by their own balloons, for no reason, in a park, while the parents don't notice. Five minutes, student-film crude, and still the purest statement of his comic physics: the world is soft, round, and hostile.

A boy and his balloon.

metas.name: Rejected
metas.description:
Captures an animator's commissioned ad cartoons being rejected one by one as they — and he — visibly fall apart. It starts with a banana announcing "my spoon is too big" and ends with the paper universe collapsing, blood pooling in the margins. Oscar-nominated, quoted for a quarter century, and it still feels unstable.

In the spring of 1999, the Family Learning Channel commissioned animator Don Hertzfeldt to produce promotional segments for their network. The cartoons were completed in five weeks. The Family Learning Channel rejected all of them upon review, and they were never aired...

metas.name: The Meaning of Life
metas.description:
Captures all of evolution and human history as a twelve-minute time-lapse that refuses to land on us. Creatures morph across geological time, crowds become patterns, patterns become individuals again; the title is the dare, and the ending is the shrug the title earns.

A sprawling look at the evolution of humankind, over the course of a billion years.

metas.name: Everything Will Be OK
metas.description:
Captures Bill, an ordinary man whose days — window light, a cough, a strange feeling in the street — start arriving out of order as an unnamed illness takes his memory apart. Part one of the trilogy; alone, it's the sunniest of the three and the most quietly frightening.

A series of dark and troubling events forces Bill to reckon with the meaning of his life - or lack thereof.

metas.name: I Am So Proud of You
metas.description: Captures Bill's family history told as a hereditary weather system: a mother, a man split into two by a train, a cousin in a rocket, the same darkness handed down like furniture. Part two of the trilogy, and the one where his prose — because by now the narration is prose — peaks.

metas.name: Wisdom Teeth
metas.description:
Captures a man having a wisdom tooth pulled, and his friend asking to pull the stitches. Five minutes, one dental thread, escalating commitment to a single bad idea. The palate cleanser of the catalogue, placed here as programmed.

Nigel does his best to help with his friend's simple request.

metas.name: World of Tomorrow Episode Two: The Burden of Other People's Thoughts
metas.description:
Captures little Emily travelling into the mind of her older clone, where memories are stored as literal rooms other people have moved into. The sequel to your #469 goes inward instead of forward: identity as a house full of other people's furniture.

Emily is visited by a backup clone of herself from the even-more distant future, as they must venture into each other's psyches in order to restore the clone's deteriorating mind.

metas.name: World of Tomorrow Episode Three: The Absent Destinations of David Prime
metas.description:
Captures a time-travelling husband erased from his own timeline, sending instructions backward to a wife who no longer remembers him. The most intricate of the three episodes — a love story conducted entirely through messages left in the wrong years.

A hidden memory sends David across the far reaches of time and space to solve a deadly mystery involving his time-traveling future selves.

metas.name: Me
metas.description:
Captures a musical about a self absorbing everything it touches, in twenty-two nearly wordless minutes. His newest: a round character rolls through a hand-drawn world converting people, places and finally the film itself into more of himself. After thirty years of drawing other people's inner lives, this is the one about the ego as a closed system — a transducer with the output looped to the input.

A musical odyssey about generational trauma and the retreat of humanity into itself.

metas.name: The Station Agent
metas.description:
Captures three lonely people failing to leave each other alone. A man with dwarfism inherits a disused train depot to be solitary in; a grief-struck artist and a talkative coffee-truck man refuse the plan. Nothing is cured; company simply accumulates. Friendship as accretion, not event.

When his only friend dies, a man born with dwarfism moves to rural New Jersey to live a life of solitude, only to meet a chatty hot dog vendor and a woman dealing with her own personal loss.

metas.name: Lucky
metas.description:
Captures a 90-year-old atheist's daily routine as a complete philosophy: yoga, crosswords, a missing tortoise named President Roosevelt, the same bar, the same stool. Harry Dean Stanton's final role — old age as appetite and community rather than decline, in a desert town that has made room for him exactly as he is.

Lucky follows the spiritual journey of a 90-year-old atheist and the quirky characters that inhabit his off the map desert town.

metas.name: Challengers
metas.description:
Captures a tennis match as the only honest conversation three people can have. A wife, a husband and his ex-best friend, thirteen years of desire and ambition routed through one challenger final, the camera riding the ball. Bodies in motion, erotic and athletic at once — the contemporary register the list was missing.

Tashi, a former tennis prodigy-turned-coach, transformed her husband into a champion. But to overcome a recent losing streak and redeem himself, he'll need to face off against his former best friend--Tashi's ex-boyfriend.

metas.name: This Is Spinal Tap
metas.description:
Captures a metal band's decline documented with total, lethal courtesy. Your collection holds exactly one film tagged Satire; this is the second, and it's also the music-industry film — amps to eleven, drummers expiring, a Stonehenge set built to the wrong unit. The mockumentary as a transducer problem: every interview projects a band that no longer exists.

Spinal Tap, one of England's loudest bands, is chronicled by film director Marty DiBergi on what proves to be a fateful tour.

metas.name: The Band's Visit
metas.description:
Captures an Egyptian police orchestra stranded for one night in the wrong Israeli town, and enmity dissolving into dinner, small talk and a roller rink. Reconciliation without a summit — just people feeding their assigned enemies. The quietest film here, and the one where music does diplomacy's job.

A band comprised of members of the Egyptian police force head to Israel to play at the inaugural ceremony of an Arab arts center, only to find themselves lost in the wrong town.

metas.name: Good Bye, Lenin!
metas.description:
Captures a son rebuilding East Germany in his mother's bedroom because the truth would kill her. Forged news broadcasts, decanted pickles, a whole fake state maintained as an act of love. History in your collection is usually an indictment; here it's a forgery staged by tenderness.

In 1990, to protect his fragile mother from a fatal shock after a long coma, a young man must keep her from learning that her beloved nation of East Germany as she knew it has disappeared.

metas.name: Son of the Bride
metas.description:
Captures a burnt-out restaurateur whose father announces he wants, at last, to marry his wife of 44 years — who has Alzheimer's — in the church wedding they never had. A son restaging his parents' love while his own life is in receivership. Mid-life repair, played warm and exact.

A dissatisfied 40-year-old, separated and without time for his own daughter and girlfriend must rethink his life when his father decides to marry his mother, who suffers from Alzheimer's disease, by church.

metas.name: Gloria
metas.description:
Captures a 58-year-old divorcée in Santiago going dancing, falling into a messy affair, and refusing to shrink. Old-er age as appetite — discos, road trips, a paintball gun used with feeling. Paulina García holds every frame; the ending is a woman dancing alone because she wants to.

A story set in Santiago and centered on Gloria, a free-spirited older woman, and the realities of her whirlwind relationship with a former naval officer whom she meets out in the clubs.

metas.name: My Neighbor Totoro
metas.description:
Captures childhood before it learns to be endangered: two sisters new to the countryside, a mother in hospital kept almost off-screen, and the forest spirits who treat worry as weather. The children's happiness here is not ignorance — it's a skill the film takes seriously.

When two girls move to the country to be near their ailing mother, they have adventures with the wondrous forest spirits who live nearby.

metas.name: The Lady Eve
metas.description:
Captures a con artist falling for her mark and taking revenge for it. Barbara Stanwyck's card sharp seduces Henry Fonda's brewery heir on an ocean liner, loses him, then returns in disguise as "Lady Eve" to marry him again out of spite — and the film's sympathies stay with her throughout. Screwball at full velocity: dialogue as card tricks, pratfalls as punctuation.

A trio of classy card sharks targets a socially awkward brewery heir, until one of them falls in love with him.

metas.name: Jour de fête
metas.description:
Captures a postman trying to become a system. François, a rural French mailman, sees a newsreel of American postal efficiency and spends a festival day attempting to deliver mail at modern speed, on a bicycle, increasingly drunk. Tati's first feature — the gentle prototype of everything he later built, and a comedy about optimisation filmed by a man who plainly preferred the unoptimised world.

A village postman with no sense of humour delivers his mail via bicycle on the day the travelling fair comes to town. He is disrupted by a short film about US speed and efficiency and the playful teasing of the village folk.

metas.name: A Moment of Innocence
metas.description:
Captures a director restaging his own worst act with the man he attacked. At seventeen, Makhmalbaf stabbed a policeman during a robbery; twenty years later he casts the policeman to play himself, and a young actor to play young Makhmalbaf, and the two versions keep correcting the production. Reenactment as negotiation between two memories of the same knife — documentary, fiction and apology occupying one frame.

An Iranian policeman asks a director to make a film about a true stabbing incident involving both of them.

metas.name: Four Lions
metas.description:
Captures incompetence as the true face of zealotry. Four Sheffield would-be jihadists train, bicker, film martyrdom videos with toy guns and argue about whether bombing a mosque would radicalise the community, in a comedy that never once softens its target or its affection. The rare satire that works by making its monsters ordinary men — the horror and the humour are the same observation.

Four incompetent British terrorists from Sheffield, set out to train for and commit an act of terror.

metas.name: Hit Man
metas.description:
Captures a philosophy professor discovering his gift is performance. Gary Johnson moonlights for the police posing as a hitman for hire; each sting is a new character built from what the client expects a killer to be. Based on a true story, and secretly a film about your favourite problem: identity as a projection fitted to an observer, and what happens when the performer prefers the projection.

A professor moonlighting as a hit man of sorts for his city police department, descends into dangerous, dubious territory when he finds himself attracted to a woman who enlists his services.

metas.name: The Ballad of Buster Scruggs
metas.description:
Captures the western as a storybook that keeps turning lethal. Six chapters from a singing gunslinger to a stagecoach of the dead, framed as pages of an old cloth-bound book — tonal whiplash as structure: farce, then a prospector's idyll, then the bleakest thing the Coens have made. The genre your collection holds only eight of, sampled across its whole emotional range in one sitting.

Six tales of life and violence in the Old West, following a singing gunslinger, a bank robber, a traveling impresario, an elderly prospector, a wagon train and a perverse pair of bounty hunters.

metas.name: Do Not Expect Too Much from the End of the World
metas.description:
Captures gig work eating a person's day in real time. An exhausted production assistant drives Bucharest casting injured workers for a safety video, intercut with a 1981 Romanian film about a woman taxi driver and her own vertical TikToks as a toxic influencer parody. Two eras of the same city projected onto each other — the contemporary film, in every sense, that your list had least of.

An overworked and underpaid production assistant drives around Bucharest to shoot the casting for a workplace safety video commissioned by a multinational company.

metas.name: They Cloned Tyrone
metas.description:
Captures a conspiracy discovered by the three people least equipped to explain it. A dealer, a sex worker and a pimp in a decaying block find the same man alive after watching him die, and pull a thread that leads under the neighbourhood. Blaxploitation styling over a genuinely paranoid systems plot — funny until the moment the mechanism's scale lands, then funny again, differently.

A series of eerie events thrusts an unlikely trio onto the trail of a nefarious government conspiracy in this pulpy mystery caper.

metas.name: Castaway on the Moon
metas.description:
Captures two solitudes becoming visible to each other across a river. A man survives a suicide jump and builds a castaway life on an uninhabited Han River island in the middle of Seoul; a hikikomori girl photographs him through a telephoto lens from her bedroom, her first contact with anyone in years. Urban isolation solved not by society but by one observer, one observed, and messages written in sand.

A failed suicide attempt leads a heartbroken man to live a life in the wilderness.

metas.name: You, the Living
metas.description:
Captures ordinary misery arranged into perfect tableaux. Fifty short scenes — a psychiatrist who's stopped believing, a girl dreaming of marrying a rock star, a carpet seller, a tuba ruining a marriage — shot in fixed frames of grey-green precision, each a small diorama of someone waiting for life to start. Deadpan as compassion: nobody is mocked, everybody is framed beautifully, nothing is resolved.

Humankind's greatness, baseness, joy, sorrow, self-confidence, anxiety, desire to love and be loved.

metas.name: Wadjda
metas.description:
Captures a girl who wants a bicycle in a country where girls don't ride them. Ten-year-old Wadjda in Riyadh hustles — mix tapes, bracelets, a Quran competition's prize money — toward a green bicycle, while her mother faces being replaced by a second wife. The first Saudi feature directed by a woman, some of it shot from inside a van because she couldn't be seen directing men in the street; the film's making is inside its meaning.

An enterprising Saudi girl signs on for her school's Koran recitation competition as a way to raise the remaining funds she needs in order to buy the green bicycle that has captured her interest.

metas.name: Smiles of a Summer Night
metas.description:
Captures Bergman being funny, which turns out to mean Bergman being exact about desire instead of death. Couples mismatched by age and appetite rotate through a country weekend engineered by a grandmother and a bottle of wine; by dawn the pairings have re-sorted. The light register of the director your list knows at his heaviest — proof the same precision plays as farce.

In Sweden at the turn of the century, members of the upper class and their servants find themselves in a romantic tangle that they try to work out amidst jealousy and heartbreak.

metas.name: The Big Short
metas.description:
Captures a true signal that nobody could afford to believe. A handful of outsiders read the US housing market correctly — the loans were fraudulent, the bonds were poison, the ratings were bought — and discover that being right early looks identical to being wrong, and costs the same. The companion piece to Inside Job: that film shows the machine, this one shows what the machine does to accurate information.

Prior to the 2008 financial crisis, a group of investors bet against the US mortgage market and are stunned by the corruption they uncover through their research.
